=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- .claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md:12,15,187-191 (and byte-identical twin workflow-templates/.claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md) | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  PROBLEM: Issue-mode cleanup is deferred until after Step 1 reads the plan, but Step 1 does not invoke it and the cleanup header still assigns it to Step 0, so stopped stage sessions can remain unarchived after `/reclarify`.
  WHY: The highest reported severity is BLOCKER; DeepSeek rated the same runtime issue MAJOR, while GLM-5.2 found no current runtime failure and rated the related header risk NIT.
- .claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md:108,191 | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: Issue-mode stop and cleanup sequences have no defined failure handling for transient errors in `set_session_title` or the issue label read.
  WHY: A rename failure may leave a title that cleanup does not match, and a label-read failure may skip archival without surfacing an error.
- .claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md:12,192 | severity=low | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: A plan without a `Source issue:` line skips issue-mode cleanup without logging or reporting that skip.
  WHY: Operators cannot distinguish an intentional skip from cleanup that was forgotten or failed to trigger.
- .claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md:187 | severity=low | confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: The cleanup header does not acknowledge the issue-mode timing exception, leaving a documentation precision gap that could enable a future regression.
  WHY: GLM-5.2 reports no runtime failure on the current head; its concern is that the header and contract test do not preserve the exception against future edits.
- tests/test_implement_plan_claude_command.py:264 | severity=low | confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The collision check only rejects the literal phrase `blocked on issue` without an em-dash prefix and can miss slugs such as `blocked-on-issue`.
  WHY: Such a slug could match the new issue-mode title predicate while escaping the test's collision check.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===
- requirement: The cleanup must actually fire on a `/reclarify` resume after Step 1 reads the plan and the `Source issue:` identifier is available.

  EVIDENCE: Step 1 contains no cleanup invocation; the cleanup header still assigns execution to Step 0 without an issue-mode timing exception; the Step 0 text defers execution until after Step 1 but provides no Step 1 hook; the workflow-templates copy has the same reported defect.
- requirement: A contract test must pin the issue-mode cleanup trigger's placement after Step 1 reads the plan and verify the cleanup-section header distinguishes issue-mode timing.
  expected_change_site: tests/test_implement_plan_claude_command.py
  confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  EVIDENCE: `test_issue_mode_archives_stopped_stage_sessions` checks text-string existence but does not pin the cleanup invocation after Step 1 or the header's timing exception; GLM-5.2 reports that the explicit deferral exists and the implementation is functionally complete, but also identifies the missing regression coverage.
- requirement: When Step 1 reads a plan without a `Source issue:` header line, the issue-mode cleanup must log/report the skip or document it as an intentional no-op.
  expected_change_site: .claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md Step 0 bullet and Zombie-checker cleanup section
  confidence=[4]

  expected_change_site: docs/INVENTORY.md Scripts section or tests/inventory_exemptions.txt
  confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]

=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- .claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md (and byte-identical twin workflow-templates/.claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md)
  Line or code reference: line 12 (new Step 0 child bullet), line 15 (Step 1), line 187 (Zombie-checker cleanup section header)
  Problem: The issue-mode cleanup requires the `Source issue: <owner>/<repo>#<N>` identifier from the plan header and the `<slug>` derived from the plan filename, both available only after Step 1 reads the plan. The Step 0 bullet at line 12 defers execution ("once step 1 has read the plan") but Step 1 contains no instruction to invoke it. The cleanup-section header at line 187 still says "Every stage session runs this in step 0, after resume hygiene" with no issue-mode timing exception. An unattended session that runs the cleanup in Step 0 will not have `<slug>` set yet, so the issue-mode cleanup's title-matching clause (line 190: "title starts with `implement-plan <slug> — `") will match no stopped sessions. The session may then proceed through Step 1 and Step 2 without ever returning to run the cleanup, leaving the stopped `— blocked on issue` session unarchived after `/reclarify` resume — exactly the bug the PR is meant to fix.
  PROBLEM: The issue-mode cleanup is deferred until after Step 1 reads the plan, but Step 1 does not invoke it and the cleanup header still assigns it to Step 0.
  WHY: An unattended session can proceed through Step 1 and Step 2 without running the cleanup, leaving the stopped session unarchived.
  severity=high | confidence=[4]
- .claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md (and byte-identical twin workflow-templates/.claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md)
  Line or code reference: line 190 (new "Issue mode: stopped stage sessions." sub-bullet)
  Problem: The cleanup predicates against the zombie-checker section header (line 187: "step 0") while the issue-mode deferral text (line 12) says "once step 1 has read the plan". The effective execution timing for this new cleanup logic is left to model interpretation of prose rather than an operational instruction.
  PROBLEM: The new cleanup logic has no documented invocation guarantee after Step 1.
  WHY: The trigger mechanism is prose-only, so an unattended session may never execute the cleanup.
  severity=high | confidence=[4]
- Requirement: "The Zombie-checker cleanup ran only from inside resume hygiene, so it never ran on this path." (PR description cause 2). The fix's contract is that the cleanup fires on a `/reclarify` resume after Step 1 reads the plan.
  Expected change site: .claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md Step 1 (after "Read" in full) — an explicit instruction to run the Zombie-checker cleanup when the plan header has a `Source issue:` line; OR the cleanup-section header at line 187 revised to acknowledge the issue-mode timing exception.
  Evidence of absence: Step 1 (line 15) contains no reference to the Zombie-checker cleanup or issue-mode cleanup. The cleanup-section header at line 187 is unchanged and still reads "Every stage session runs this in step 0, after resume hygiene" with no exception for issue-mode timing. The deferral text at line 12 describes the cleanup but provides no operational instruction in Step 1 to invoke it. The workflow-templates copy is byte-identical and carries the same defect. The contract test at tests/test_implement_plan_claude_command.py:245-260 checks text-string existence but does not assert that Step 1 invokes the cleanup, that the cleanup header distinguishes issue-mode timing, or that a deferred trigger has a matching operational hook after Step 1.
  severity=high | confidence=[4]
- Requirement: A contract test must pin the issue-mode cleanup trigger's placement relative to Step 1 and verify the cleanup-section header distinguishes issue-mode timing, so a future edit cannot silently regress the trigger.
  Expected change site: tests/test_implement_plan_claude_command.py — extend test_issue_mode_archives_stopped_stage_sessions (or add a sibling test).
  Evidence of absence: test_issue_mode_archives_stopped_stage_sessions (lines 245-260) only checks text-string existence. It does not assert that Step 1 invokes cleanup, does not assert the cleanup-section header at line 187 distinguishes issue-mode timing, and does not pin the deferred trigger to an operational hook after Step 1. A future edit that re-orders bullets, strips the deferral text, or revises the header could restore the bug with no failing test.
  severity=low | confidence=[3]
=== END FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===

=== FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===
- .claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md
  Line or code reference: Step 0 bullet (line 12), Step 1 (line 15), cleanup-section header (line 187)
  Problem: The cleanup trigger for issue-mode resume is deferred until Step 1 reads the plan, but no operational instruction invokes it after Step 1, and the cleanup-section header incorrectly assigns it to Step 0.
  Why it fails at runtime: The unattended session follows Step 0 first. It will attempt cleanup without the Source issue: identifier (resulting in no-op or error) or it will defer per text but never execute the deferred cleanup because Step 1 provides no hook. The stopped session remains unarchived, leaving idle sessions in the list.
  severity=critical | confidence=[5]
- .claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md
  Line or code reference: line 108 (Issue-mode stop rename), line 191 (Cleanup label-read)
  Problem: The issue-mode stop and cleanup sequences lack defined failure handling paths for transient errors in set_session_title (rename) or mcp__github__issue_read (label-read).
  Why it fails at runtime: A rename failure can leave the session with its old title (which cleanup does not match), and a label-read failure can skip archival without surfacing an error to the operator, requiring manual intervention.
  severity=high | confidence=[4]
- .claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md
  Line or code reference: Step 0 child bullet, line 12; cleanup-section report line 192
  Problem: A plan that lacks a Source issue: header line skips cleanup without logging or reporting the skip.
  Why it fails at runtime: Operators cannot distinguish an intentional skip from cleanup that was forgotten, failed to trigger, or was misapplied because the report line only fires when m (count of archived sessions) is computable, so an issue-mode resume without a Source issue: line never produces a count or log.
  severity=low | confidence=[4]
